text:
lee: Heads-up — our OTLP ingest spiked this morning (12x) and cost alerts fired. Any quick ideas on sampling we can roll without losing error/latency visibility?

maria: ouch. where are most spans coming from? route-level? background jobs?

lee: mostly API routes for /generate and /embeddings. small fraction from batch jobs. tail of long-running requests is noisy.

oliver: i'd push for hybrid: head sampling to keep early request traces and tail sampling to keep high-latency/error traces. keep 100% for error spans.

jamie: agree on hybrid. also we should dynamic-sample by customer_tier — enterprise gets higher retention. cheaper tenants sampled more.

zara: important: exporters matter. Honeycomb pricing is per event, Datadog per span, and S3/OTEL-collector to BigQuery is cheaper but means more infra. so sampling must be enforced at collector, not SDK.

patrick: +1 on enforcing at collector. SDK-level sampling is nice but can be bypassed by clients. we need consistent downstream quotas.

lee: can someone sketch a small policy? thinking: default head sample 1% for low tier, 5% for mid, 25% for enterprise; tail-sample keep all spans with duration > 500ms or any span with error=true. also keep all spans for flagged routes (/billing, /account).

maria: sketch:
```
# pseudo policy applied in otel-collector processor
policy = {
  "head_sample": {"low": 0.01, "mid": 0.05, "enterprise": 0.25},
  "tail_threshold_ms": 500,
  "always_keep_routes": ["/billing","/account"],
  "preserve_error": true
}
for span in incoming_spans:
  if span.attributes.get('error'):
    export(span)
  elif span.duration_ms >= policy.tail_threshold_ms:
    export(span)
  else:
    sample_prob = policy.head_sample[get_tier(span.attributes['customer_tier'])]
    if random() < sample_prob:
      export(span)
```

oliver: looks good. couple notes: 1) need to define how to tag spans with customer_tier at the edge (auth middleware). 2) maintain deterministic sampling for a trace (sample by trace_id hash) so partial traces don't get exported.

jamie: +1 on deterministic trace sampling. also we should record sampling decision as an attribute so console dashboards show sampled vs unsampled traffic. e.g., sampling.decision = "head|tail|kept-error"

zara: retention tiers: raw spans for enterprise 30d, mid 14d, low 7d. store sampled raw spans in hot storage for 48h then archive to cold. this reduces cost.

patrick: exporter config: prefer OTLP->otel-collector with sampling processor, then export to two sinks: real-time telemetry (Datadog/honeycomb) for 1P metrics/alerts and long-term S3 for bulk analytics. batch + retry critical.

lee: concern: we use per-route routing policies for requests already. can we piggyback routing decisions to set sampling bucket? e.g., route metadata tells collector the initial sample weight.

maria: yes, middleware can attach attributes: telemetry.route_priority and telemetry.sample_hint. collector uses that. but we must verify no PII leaks. scrub sensitive attrs before exporter.

oliver: also watch tail sampling with distributed traces: if one service keeps all tail spans but upstream was dropped by head sample, we might end up with incomplete traces. deterministic sampling at trace root helps. consider stateful tail-sampling processor that buffers trace fragments for N seconds to decide.

jamie: buffering tradeoffs: more memory and latency in collector. we can make buffer window adaptive by route SLO. short window for low-latency routes, longer for background flows.

zara: we should run a 2-week canary: implement collector sampling + deterministic trace hash + tagging. compare error-rate signal fidelity on a handful of routes. dashboard to show sampling ratios and retained errors.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: otel-collector-sampling-v0.1 -> staging at 2024-06-19T03:00Z by @oliver.

patrick: also add a metrics exporter for sampling_decisions: count_by(route, customer_tier, decision). feed into console to drive automatic suggestions in Optimize.

lee: great. action items: (1) oliver add collector sampling processor PR with deterministic trace sampling + config UI fields; (2) jamie instrument middleware to tag customer_tier and route metadata; (3) zara prepare retention plan and cost projection; (4) maria run 2-week canary on /generate and /embeddings. i'll own dashboards.

maria: ping on PRs in #eng-releases when ready.

oliver: will do. starting draft now.

zara: i'll model costs with current ingest numbers and three retention tiers, share spreadsheet.

lee: thanks everyone. keep thread updated — if we see unexpected drop in error signals we rollback sampling at collector. :thumbsup:
